thread:
ashley.support: Hey team — urgent escalation for a Private/VPC customer. Production app started getting 502s and 401s to the Redwood API around 08:12 UTC. They see intermittent CONNECT resets and some requests show an auth failure even though tokens are valid.

ashley.support: Customer says this only happens from behind their corporate egress proxy (we're in a VPC with an egress allowlist to their corp proxy). Direct curl from dev laptop to our API works fine.

diego.sre: Can you paste the failing request log + any client-side trace? Also need tcpdump of the CONNECT flow if possible.

ashley.support: Pasting sanitized logs from customer (they obfuscated hostnames):
```
2024-06-03T08:11:59Z request_id=abc123 method=POST path=/v1/chat status=502 backend_error="upstream: connection reset by peer"
2024-06-03T08:12:05Z request_id=abc124 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=401 auth_error="token invalid"
```
They also provided a curl run from inside their VPC via proxy: 
```
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.local:8080 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
* Connected to corp-proxy.local (10.10.0.5) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.ai:443\n> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive\n> \n< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (10.20.30.40) port 443 (#1)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1): (truncated)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
They also ran openssl s_client through the proxy and noted the ClientHello looked weird (no server_name).
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -proxy corp-proxy.local:8080 -servername api.redwood.ai -tlsextdebug -msg
---
*** ClientHello, no extension server_name found
```

maria.network: If ClientHello from client lacks SNI, many transparent proxies that do TLS interception will fail or downgrade to MITM mode and re-sign. But the openssl call explicitly set -servername; odd that proxy strips it. Any chance the proxy is doing an explicit CONNECT + TLS-intercept where it terminates and re-originates TLS?

ivan.engineering: Another clue: customer captured the upstream headers after the proxy. Their backend shows our Authorization header turned into: `Proxy-Authorization: Bearer REDACTED` and our original Authorization was removed on some requests. That would explain sporadic 401s.

ashley.support: So two issues: 1) CONNECT/TLS interception is removing/stripping SNI (handshake shows missing server_name), causing backend TLS mismatch or proxy failing to forward host. 2) Proxy is rewriting Authorization -> Proxy-Authorization or dropping header, causing 401s. Both would produce the symptoms.

diego.sre: Steps to repro locally: set up a tiny HTTP CONNECT proxy that can optionally strip SNI or rewrite headers. But first, can customer give us tcpdump of the 3-way exchange (client->proxy via CONNECT, proxy->server) with packet captures showing TLS ClientHello bytes pre- and post-proxy? If they can run: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/proxy-conn.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443
```
Also ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -proxy corp-proxy:8080 -tlsextdebug` and attach full output.

maria.network: Quick workaround while they engage their infra team: 1) Configure SDK to use an explicit TLS tunnel that sets SNI in the outer layer? (not always possible). 2) Route traffic via a different egress that does straight NAT rather than corporate proxy (if they have an alternate egress). 3) Ask their network team to enable TLS passthrough for api.redwood.ai on the proxy, or disable header rewriting for Authorization for our host.

ivan.engineering: From the runtime side we can also add a more explicit fallback: if upstream returns 502 after CONNECT success, retry once after a short jitter. But that’s just mitigation; header rewrite causing 401 must be fixed on their side.

ashley.support: Customer sent the tcpdump. I ran a quick `tshark -r` and compared bytes. The CLIENT->PROXY ClientHello contains SNI and extensions. The PROXY->DEST ClientHello (the one originating from proxy after CONNECT) lacks server_name. They appear to be performing a re-originating ClientHello and not forwarding the original. tcpdump snippets: 
```
# client->proxy: ClientHello extension type 0x00 - server_name: api.redwood.ai
# proxy->dest: ClientHello extension missing server_name
```

maria.network: That confirms proxy is acting as TLS-intercepting gateway and not injecting SNI in the re-originated handshake. Many proxies will set the target hostname but some LD/edge configs intentionally strip SNI to force name-based blocking. They might also substitute certificate SANs which could trigger our runtime to reject cert chain if CN mismatch.

ashley.support: Customer asked if we can accept connections by IP to avoid SNI requirements. Not really — our deploys use SNI for host routing and TLS cert selection.

diego.sre: Action items for customer (send to their network team):
- Allow CONNECT tunneling to api.redwood.ai:443 without terminating TLS (enable passthrough) OR configure their TLS-terminating proxy to preserve server_name extension on re-originated handshakes.
- Disable header rewriting for Authorization for that destination or add an explicit passthrough rule so Authorization is not moved to Proxy-Authorization.
- If they must MITM, ensure the proxy presents a cert that includes api.redwood.ai in SAN and that it preserves expected headers.
- Provide pcaps of both sides of the proxy (client->proxy and proxy->server) and the proxy config if possible.

ivan.engineering: We'll add a short-term SDK telemetry flag the customer can enable to log a one-off debug for failed requests (non-sensitive: status codes, proxied host, whether CONNECT returned 200, but not tokens). That might help root cause if they can't share pcaps.

ashley.support: Customer is looping in their infra/security ops. They've opened a ticket with the proxy vendor. They also said the proxy has a rule that collapses SNI for certain allowedlists to prevent host leakage — eg it intentionally strips server_name for privacy.

maria.network: If it's intentional (privacy feature), then the only fix is to allow passthrough for our host or put Redwood on their egress allowlist as a TLS passthrough destination. Otherwise you get one of: handshake failures, wrong certs, or the proxy re-originated handshake without SNI which breaks routing.

ashley.support: I'll keep thread updated. Next steps: customer to provide pcaps + proxy config + vendor bug ref. SRE/eng will prepare telemetry hook (ivan) and a short KB we can send to enterprise customers about proxy behaviours that break CONNECT (diego/maria).

kubedeploy-bot: deploy status: no relevant deploys during window 2024-06-03 08:00-09:00 UTC.

ashley.support: Thanks all. Customer will update once infra team confirms passthrough rule or vendor fix. :thumbsup:
_notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread for support escalation around HTTP CONNECT proxy interference (SNI stripping and header rewrites). Messages are short, realistic, include logs and commands, and suggested action items.
